prompt: A panoramic illustration shows a tight cluster of four gleaming corporate campuses—not a geographic frontier but the handful of firms racing to train the largest general-purpose models—each rising above cavernous halls of specialised chips whose glowing racks consume energy on the scale of a national science budget; inside, researchers stare half-comprehending at a vast, swirling black-box system whose capabilities erupt in sudden luminous leaps, while money and soaring stock tickers pour in and competing American and Chinese flags streak across the sky; protesters cluster at the glass office doors waving signs about loss of control and military use, a distant university seminar hall stands empty, and government figures linger at the edges, hands raised yet motionless, embodying the fusion of research ambition, private profit and great-power rivalry that keeps them from slowing the pace-setters.
